title: Can you see which ants are carrying food?
question: In which of these can you pick out the ants that are carrying a load — and does the difference between a light load and a full one read at all?
context_md:
You said the real answer was **anything visually interesting**, and named *"visual collection of food (although this might just be a coloration thing)"*. It was invisible: what an ant is carrying is internal state that has never been drawn.

Same world, same frame, same seed. **Only the colour rule differs** — nothing about the simulation changed between these three.

**Two things I measured, so you don't have to take them on trust:**

- **"Carrying food" is not an event.** 34 of the 38 ants are holding food at this instant, and none is below a quarter-full. So a simple on/off cue would paint nearly the whole colony one colour and tell you nothing. What actually varies is *how heavy the load is*, so these show it in three steps: faint, medium, strong.
- **The cue does fire, and hard** — it repaints 1,664 pixels by up to 171 levels. So if you cannot see it, that is about legibility against this bed, not about the rule being broken.

**What I am unsure about, and why this is a three-way rather than a before/after:** the ground line here is already crowded with pale litter, stems and seed cells, so making an ant *brighter* may just make it look like more litter. The other candidate ignores that and uses a colour nothing else in the bed wears. I expect you may find it garish — say so and I will pull it back; **the question I am stuck on is only whether you can see them at all.**

One thing worth looking for either way: the ants are not only on the ground. Some are up in the herbs.
